motions.motion: continue the request for a Conditional Use Permit for Weyburn Retreat PUD located at 1306 Spring Lane. The following information was sought: 1. Provide adequate parking on site. 2. Provide information on the continuance of the sidewalk design. 3. Provide specifics of a Shared Maintenance Agreement. 4. Provide additional information on the moving of utilities with the goal being to widen the road to 22 feet

approve the Conditional Use Permit for the Cotton Bottom Restaurant and Bar at 6252 South Holladay Boulevard subject to the following: Findings: 1. The use complies with the LU zone. 2. The proposal will enhance the viability of the site and provide enhances sales and property tax benefits to the City. 3. The general public has asked for the city to retain this use for a number of years. 4. The use as proposed complies with the Request for Proposal issued by the City for this property. 5. The Cotton Bottom project as proposed complies with the specific requirement of Section 13.08 of the Holladay Code regarding conditional use as follows. a. It is consistent with policies set forth in the city's general plan applicable to the site where the conditional use will be located. b. It is allowed by the zone regulations where the conditional use will be located. c. It is compatible with the character of the site, adjacent properties and uses, and existing development within the vicinity of the site where the use will be located. d. It provides vehicular access to the site without materially degrading the existing level of service of the abutting streets. e. Has all driveways oriented to direct traffic to streets, major or local, without impacting the safety, purpose, and character of these streets. f. May have street-side parking for the proposed use, in areas of the site that will not adversely impact the reasonable use of adjacent properties. g. Will accommodate peak traffic to the site without impairing the use and enjoyment of adjacent properties. City of Holladay Planning Commission Meeting - 05/05/2020 8 h. It provides an internal circulation system designed to mitigate adverse impacts on the adjacent property from motorized, nonmotorized, and pedestrian traffic. i. Will, upon PC imposed requirements have restricted hours of operation of the proposed conditional use in relation to the hours of activity or operation of other nearby uses to mitigate noise, light, odor, or other nuisances that unreasonably impair the use and enjoyment of adjacent properties. j. Has or will have existing or proposed utility and public services will be adequate to support the proposed use at normal service levels and is designed in a manner to avoid adverse impacts on adjacent land uses, public services, and utility resources. k. Will have appropriate buffering, such as landscaping, setbacks, and building location, to protect adjacent land uses from light, noise, and visual impacts result. Also, this use will not: a. Contribute to a detrimental concentration of existing nonconforming or conditional uses substantially similar to the use proposed within one- fourth (1/4) mile of the exterior boundary of the subject property; b. Result in loss of privacy, objectionable views of large parking or storage areas; or views or sounds of loading and unloading areas; and c. Encroach on or cause erosion of the bank of a river or stream, or direct runoff into a river or stream without approval by the appropriate stormwater authority. Conditions: 1. The use must obtain all applicable licenses from the State of Utah DABC, the City of Holladay, Salt Lake County, and any other applicable entity which has jurisdiction over this use. 2. Hours of operation for outdoor use shall be limited to 10:00 p.m. as determined by the DABC and the City of Holladay. 3. Operation of the parking and patio areas shall be done in a manner to minimize overcrowding the parking areas, public streets, and negatively impacting surrounding residential property abutting restaurants and Knudsen Park. 4. Significant changes to the use must be approved by the City of Holladay zoning ordinance. City of Holladay Planning Commission Meeting - 05/05/2020 9 5. The hours of operation for the internal use shall be as per the DABC hours of operation. 6. Keep the Cotton Bottom name and logo

approve the preliminary site plan for Cotton Bottom based on the following: Findings: 1. The site plan complies with the requirements of the Holladay Zoning ordinance and with the approved checklists for this development with the exception of a few minor items that can be handled at staff level (TRC) after this approval. Conditions: 1. Submittal and resolution by the applicant of minor remaining items identified by the TRC at staff level in preparation for final approval. 2. Delegate final site plan approval to the Technical Review Committee (“TRC”) but not until all preliminary site plan items are complete
motions.result: ordinance and with the approved checklists for this development with the exception of a few minor items that can be handled at staff level (TRC) after this approval.
The motion passed with the unanimous consent of the Commission.
